articles.title: As Ukraine Struggles With Air Defence Weapons, India Develops A Strong Eco-system
articles.description: Ukraine’s F-16 fleet is facing mounting pressure from maintenance bottlenecks and shortages of air-to-air missiles. More than half of the aircraft are reportedly in maintenance limbo, while high operational tempo is increasing flight hours and further straining the support network. Ukraine has received around 40-50 F-16s, with additional aircraft promised by European countries, but shortages of AIM-9 Sidewinders and AIM-120 AMRAAMs have reportedly forced pilots to ration missiles and rely more on the 20mm cannon. The experience highlights the importance of sustaining both aircraft and weapons during prolonged conflict. For India, this underlines the significance of its indigenous Astra air-to-air missile programme. Developed by DRDO and integrated with the Su-30MKI, Astra Mk-I entered production under a Rs 2,971-crore contract with Bharat Dynamics Limited. India has also tested an indigenous RF seeker for Astra, with two missiles successfully destroying aerial targets. The programme involves more than 50 public and private industries, strengthening India's control over missile supply, replenishment and future upgrades.#Ukraine #F16 #F16FighterJet #AstraMissile #AstraMk1 #AstraAAM #AirToAirMissile #AIM9Sidewinder #AIM120AMRAAM #DRDO

articles.title: Govt proposes tougher penalties for petroleum offences, decriminalises licence breaches
articles.description: The Indian government has proposed amendments to the Petroleum Act, aimed at decriminalizing regulatory breaches. Violations of petroleum licence terms may incur civil penalties instead of criminal charges, promoting a more administrative approach. However, serious offences related to public safety will still face criminal prosecution under existing laws. The draft amendments outline significant penalties for various violations, including severe fines and imprisonment.
